summary: Tested new 'Sign in with Google' (Emergent-managed OAuth) integration coexisting with JWT email/password login. Backend endpoint POST /api/auth/google/session validated via 8 pytest cases (invalid session_id → 401, missing body/field → 422, JWT login regression + /api/auth/me + wrong password). Frontend validated: Google button visible with correct copy + separator, initial redirect URL uses window.location.origin dynamically (captured via request interception), AuthCallback component renders on /dashboard#session_id=fake and correctly handles 401 with error toast + redirect to /login, email/password login regression works and stores atlas_token in localStorage. All 8 backend + 4 frontend flows PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: Endpoint /api/auth/google/session correctly (a) uses case-insensitive email match via regex, (b) excludes MongoDB _id via projection, (c) denies unregistered emails with 403 and clear Spanish message, (d) auto-links google_linked=true + picture on success, (e) issues own JWT via create_access_token({'sub': email}) reusing existing auth infra. Good code quality.

Frontend LoginPage handleGoogleLogin correctly uses window.location.origin + '/dashboard' (NOT hardcoded) as required by Emergent Auth playbook. Verified via request interception: redirect goes to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<encoded-origin>/dashboard.
AuthCallback uses useRef guard (hasProcessed) to prevent double-processing under React StrictMode double-render — good defensive coding.
AuthContext.loginWithGoogleSession stores JWT under same key 'atlas_token' as email/password login, so downstream axios interceptors and route guards work unchanged. Clean design.

Minor: /api/auth/google/session accepts empty string session_id (Pydantic passes it) which then fails upstream with 401 (not 422). Acceptable, but a Field(min_length=1) constraint would return 422 earlier for consistency. Not blocking.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing seeded admin user.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google OAuth end-to-end with a real Google account is NOT testable in automation (requires real Google login). Coverage achieved: (a) backend endpoint handles 401/422/403 branches — validated via curl-equivalent pytest with fake session_id; (b) frontend Google button + redirect URL construction — validated via request interception; (c) AuthCallback error path (401 from backend) — validated end-to-end; (d) success path (200 from backend + JWT storage) validated via code review + JWT login regression that uses the SAME create_access_token function. If E1 needs to change anything, retest test_google_auth.py + /app/backend/tests/test_batch_upload_concurrency.py.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no issues found. Both auth flows (email/password + Google OAuth) work as designed per user's decisions: (1) both methods coexist, (2) unregistered emails → 403, (3) existing emails → auto-linked via google_linked=true. The JWT emission is unified so existing route guards and axios auth headers work transparently.
